profile.instrument: a 1978 sunburst Fender Precision called The Cinder
profile.commute: a white Ford Transit van with a broken passenger door handle

memories.text: Cut five tracks in one afternoon at Blue Fern in Decatur and the whole session ran on a click at ninety-two beats per minute.
The Nakamichi BX-100 has been in pieces on my kitchen table for eleven days and the new belts are still sitting in the envelope unopened.
Decided to move The Cinder from flatwounds to half-rounds for this record, because the flats were disappearing under the organ in the low mids.
The van's passenger door handle finally came off in the drummer's hand outside the venue and he handed it to me like a relay baton.
The producer, Nnamdi, asked me to play the whole bridge with my thumb instead of a pick, and he was right, so I did not tell him he was right.
I drink ginger beer with no ice at every session because ice makes the can sweat onto the charts.
Called my mum in Lagos on Sunday morning and she walked me through the plantain again, insisting the oil has to smell like nothing before the first slice goes in.
Played a wedding in Marietta where the bride's father sang two songs with us and the second one was in Twi and nobody had the chart.
Decided to turn down the six-week tour because it overlaps the record dates, and told my agent to keep me clear through the end of September.
Found a boxed Sony WM-D6C at an estate sale in Kirkwood and the seller thought it was a phone charger.
The Cinder has a cigarette burn on the upper horn that was there when I bought it in 2009 and I have never once considered refinishing it.
Broke a D string on take nine, which I have not done in about four years, and finished the take on the remaining three because the drummer would not stop.
Decided to track the whole record through the old Ampeg B-15 with a ribbon mic a foot back, and to stop bothering with the direct signal entirely.
Told the engineer the room hum was coming from the fridge in the lounge and not the amp, and we tracked the rest of the afternoon with the fridge unplugged.
Drove home down I-285 with the windows open because the van's air conditioning has been dead since June, and I still made it in twenty-five minutes.
Restrung The Cinder with the new half-rounds at eight in the morning and let them settle for an hour before I even plugged in.
There are seven charts in the folder for today's session and only two of them have the bass part actually written out.
Nnamdi texted to say the singer wants the second verse dropped a whole tone, so I spent lunch rewriting my part in D flat and complaining about it.
